messages:
alice: Heads-up — telemetry from last night's rollout shows latency spikes when small micro-windows get merged into larger cohorts during a high-churn period. Noticed ~120ms tail increases for a subset of requests.
ben: Can you paste the graph? rough time range? :thinking:
alice: Sure — zoomed in: 02:13–02:22 UTC. Spikes coincide with two cohort-merge events and a quick prefeth surge. Link: https://toast.internal/plots/lotta_lines (redacted)
carlos: That's the pattern we expected but hoped our soft-isolation would hide it. Is this the same as the merge path where we combine cohort A (tiny) into cohort B (large) instead of keeping A separate?
alice: Exactly. We had smallwindow A (avg 5 tokens) merge into B (avg 120 tokens) because merge threshold hit. The KV warmup + packing bumped Coalesce window and the big cohort pulled others into its deadline corridor.
diane: Do we have logs that show the admission decision? paste from the admission daemon:

```
[02:13:05] admit: cohort_id=42 size=3 tokens=15 deadline_ms=20
[02:13:05] merge: target_cohort=7 size_after=128 deadline_ms=200
[02:13:06] dispatch: batch_id=9001 exec_path=longtail_fastpath
```

ben: That dispatch path into longtail_fastpath is the issue — those tiny requests hit the slower kernel because reordering destroyed the fastpath alignment.
eve: Observed memory pressure on that worker too. When the big cohort got scheduled it filled the slab and small requests had to wait for KV availability. We saw a couple of OOM-ish GC pauses (not OS OOM) during the window.
frank: From product POV: user-facing latency jumps are the main concern. We prefer fix that reduces tail regressions even if unit cost slightly increases.
carlos: Options I see:
  1) Change merge heuristic: require token-size-homogeneity ratio < X to merge. (Keep tiny windows separate.)
  2) Deterministic merge ordering: prefer merging small->small or big->big only.
  3) Early fastpath pin: if a request qualifies for micro-fastpath, refuse merge into any cohort that would force a fallback kernel.
  4) Soft headroom credits: reserve N slots per cohort for micro-requests to avoid starvation.
  5) Dynamic fallback: if merge would increase 95p by >Y ms (predicted from model), skip.

Which is least invasive?
alice: (3) + (1) seems low-risk. Fastpath pin is a small admission check; ratio threshold we already have but bumping it might be OK. (4) touches allocator which is invasive.
diane: Agree. Implementation sketch for (3): add a flag on enqueue: `fastpath_eligibility=true`. In merger, if target cohort has any member with `fastpath_eligibility=false` then we mark resulting cohort as `fastpath_disabled` and avoid merging fastpath-eligible requests into that cohort.
ben: Small PR surface but we need to ensure we don't create too many singletons. Could add a cooldown that forces attempted re-merge after T seconds.
eve: We also should add metrics: `merge_skipped_due_to_fastpath`, `cohort_fastpath_disabled_ratio`, and instrument the dispatch kernel chooser to log when a fastpath-eligible request ends up on fallback.
carlos: For the ratio threshold change, propose config `merge_token_ratio_limit=8` (i.e., if max/min token count > 8 skip). We can tune.
frank: How will this affect cost? Rough estimate?
alice: Early estimate: more micro-batches -> 4–8% higher per-token compute cost in synthetic tests, but 95p latency down ~30–50ms for affected shapes.
diane: Edge case: what about repeated tiny requests from same tenant flooding tiny-cohort pool? We risk creating starvation across cohorts.
carlos: That's where cooldown + soft headroom combine: pin fastpath but also track per-tenant micro-burst credits. If a tenant burns credits, allow merge temporarily.en: Suggested step plan:
  - quick telemetry patch + metrics (1 day)
  - implement fastpath_eligibility guard in admission + merge (2 days)
  - add cooldown + config defaults (1 day)
  - A/B rollout to 10% then 50% with telemetry (3–5 days)
alice: Sounds good. I'll file a lightweight RFC note for the change and link the testing plan. @deploy-bot can you add a canary for the admission change? :pray:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: admission/fastpath-guard v0.1 -> canary cluster alpha-2 at 2026-03-25T04:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
eve: I'll watch memory pressure and KV warmup metrics during canary.
frank: Let's also set a customer alert if 95p latency delta >50ms on prod after rollout.
diane: Quick question: do we need to change the kernel selector API to expose `fastpath_disabled`? Or can admission mark batch metadata only?
carlos: Admission metadata only; kernel selector already looks at batch characteristics (seq_len, token_count). We'll add `fastpath_hint` to batch proto (string) — tiny change.
alice: OK. I'll open the PRs and add a test harness that simulates mix of 5-token queries + 120-token background. Expect to iterate on merge_token_ratio.
ben: :thumbsup:
frank: Thanks team — please post perf numbers in thread as they land.
alice: will do. Closing loop once canary finishes. :lock:
